annotation.title_clean: Autonomy, artificial intelligence and robotics: Technical aspects of human control
annotation.title_en: Autonomy, artificial intelligence and robotics: Technical aspects of human control
annotation.authors_or_issuer: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
annotation.summary_en: ICRC report from a 2018 expert round-table on technical aspects of human control over autonomous systems, drawing on civilian robotics experience. It examines predictability, reliability, machine learning risks and civilian safety standards, concluding States should urgently set limits on autonomy in weapon systems and agree on required human control.
key_provisions_or_claims: Human-on-the-loop supervision requires situational awareness, time to intervene, and an intervention mechanism, and is not a panacea.
Predictability and reliability are hard to ensure for autonomous systems; operational constraints on task, environment, time and area improve predictability.
Machine learning adds unpredictability, bias and lack of explainability, heightening concerns for weapon control functions.
Civilian safety-critical standards demand human supervision, fail-safe deactivation and operational constraints.
States should urgently agree limits on autonomy and the type and degree of human control required.
